question: A strong magnet is moved towards a stationary coil. When the angle between the direction of motion of the magnet and the plane of the coil is ________, then the induced current in the coil will be minimum.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**90º**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **magnet** is moved towards a stationary coil, an **electromotive force (EMF)** is induced in the coil according to **Faraday’s Law of Electromagnetic Induction**.
 
• The magnitude of the induced current depends on the **rate of change of magnetic flux** through the coil.
 
• The **magnetic flux** through the coil is maximum when the motion of the magnet is **perpendicular (90º)** to the plane of the coil.
 
• At this angle, the **rate of change of flux linkage** is zero, which leads to a **minimum induced current** in the coil.
 
• If the magnet moves parallel to the plane of the coil (0º), there is a greater component of the magnetic flux linked to the coil, and the induced current is higher.
 
• Thus, the induced current is **minimum at 90º**, as the alignment of the magnet's motion relative to the coil does not favor significant flux linkage.
 
• This principle is widely applied in **electromagnetic devices**, such as generators and transformers, to optimize current generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Faraday’s Law of Electromagnetic Induction**__

 __
 
• States that an **EMF is induced** in a conductor when the magnetic flux linked with it changes over time.
 
• The induced EMF is directly proportional to the **rate of change of magnetic flux**.
 
• This principle is the basis for the working of devices such as **electric generators, transformers, and induction motors**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Electromagnetic Induction**__
 
 
• Electromagnetic induction is used in **power generation** by hydroelectric, thermal, and wind power plants.
 
• It is applied in **induction heating**, where electrical energy is converted to heat energy for industrial purposes.
 
• Electromagnetic induction finds application in **wireless charging technology** for devices such as smartphones and electric vehicles.
